ops.title: synckit host add reports a green mesh when the peer's SSH server swallows the remote exit status
ops.description:
`synckitd host add` treats a zero exit as proof the remote step worked. Against a
peer whose SSH server discards the remote exit status, every remote leg reads as
success, so `host add` prints a green mesh over a bootstrap that did not happen.

Measured 2026-08-07 on the live pair; every fact below was re-verified that day.

## The transport discards the remote exit status

- This laptop: `yasyf-forge.tail71af5d.ts.net`, Tailscale client 1.102.2
  (`/Applications/Tailscale.app`, the sandboxed macOS GUI build).
- The peer `yasyf-home.tail71af5d.ts.net` serves SSH from open-source
  `tailscaled` **1.98.5**, running as root (pid 1296) from
  `/usr/local/bin/tailscaled`. CORRECTION to the first report: that path is a
  root-owned symlink to a **mise**-installed build
  (`/Users/yasyf/.local/share/mise/installs/go-tailscale-com-cmd-tailscaled/v1.98.5/bin/tailscaled`),
  not a Homebrew keg. `/Applications/Tailscale.app` is absent on that box, so
  nothing there serves SSH from the GUI build.

Measured table — one `ssh` per row, remote command `/bin/sh -c 'echo RAN; exit N'`:

| remote exit | local ssh rc | stdout |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | `RAN` |
| 1 | 0 | `RAN` |
| 7 | 0 | `RAN` |
| 42 | 0 | `RAN` |
| 255 | 0 | `RAN` |

The command genuinely runs (stdout `RAN` every time). The server affirmatively
sends the wrong value rather than omitting the message: `ssh -vv` on the exit-7
row logs `debug1: Exit status 0`, with `debug1: Remote protocol version 2.0,
remote software version Tailscale` identifying the server.

## Why synckit cannot see through it

- `execSSHOnce` (`hostregistry/dial.go:134-151`) reads failure only from the
  process error `runner.Run` returns, i.e. only from the exit code.
- `isConnFailure` (`hostregistry/dial.go:156-162`) keys failover on
  `sshConnFailureExit = 255` (`dial.go:17`).

Over this transport every remote command looks successful, so the inverse-
registration guard at `daemon/bootstrap.go:102-104` can never fire and 255 dial
failover can never trigger.

(Anchor corrections against the first report: `dial.go` lives in `hostregistry/`,
not `daemon/`; `execSSHOnce` is 134-151, not 139-156; `isConnFailure` is 156-162,
not 154-160; the inverse-registration guard is bootstrap.go:102-104, not 104-107.)

## Observed end state

`synckitd host add yasyf@yasyf-home.tail71af5d.ts.net` exited 0 and printed
`registered inverse host … / reconciled … / installed services`. All three lines
were false. The peer's registry, read back on 2026-08-07, is still empty:

```
$ ssh yasyf@yasyf-home… 'python3 -c "…json.load(open(state.json))[\"host_registry\"]…"'
{ "self": "yasyf@yasyf-home.tail71af5d.ts.net", "hosts": [] }
```

(The registry lives under `host_registry` inside
`~/.config/synckit/state.json`; there is no separate `hosts.json`.)

That shape corroborates the diagnosis exactly. `AddHost` persists `g.Self` at
`daemon/bootstrap.go:46-52` **before** the `--no-recurse` branch, then fails at
`bootstrap.go:63-65`. A peer registry carrying a `self` and zero `hosts` is the
fingerprint of an inverse leg that got past line 46 and died at line 63 —
`synckitd: register yasyf@yasyf-forge…: exact remote synckitd path is
unavailable` (REMOTE_RC=1), which synckit never saw.

## Why the inverse leg failed at all (legitimate, and separately verified)

`--no-recurse` → `daemon/bootstrap.go:60-66` → `Mesh.RemoteBinaryPath`
(`hostregistry/registry.go:244-251`) → `r.SSH(ctx, target, "command -v "+binary)`
at `registry.go:245`, i.e. the peer must ssh **back** into this laptop. Nothing
listens on port 22 here (`nc -z 127.0.0.1 22` → rc 1; macOS Remote Login off).

Reproduced read-only on 2026-08-07, without mutating either registry — the peer
ssh-ing back at this laptop under synckit's own dial options:

```
ssh yasyf@yasyf-home… 'ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=3 \
  -o ServerAliveInterval=5 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 \
  yasyf@yasyf-forge… "command -v synckitd"; echo "PEER_SAW_RC=$?"'
→ ssh: connect to host yasyf-forge.tail71af5d.ts.net port 22: Operation timed out
→ PEER_SAW_RC=255
→ local rc = 0
```

The peer saw 255. The outer ssh — the one synckit rides — reported 0. That is the
whole defect in four lines: the failure is real, correctly detected one hop away,
and erased on the way back.

**The closed port is expected and correct. The defect is that synckit reported
success anyway.**

## Question for the owner, not a prescription

The natural shape is to **corroborate the registration** — read the peer's
registry back after the inverse leg and assert the expected host is in it —
rather than trusting an exit code the transport is free to fabricate. Open
questions:

1. Is corroboration-after-mutation the right general contract for every remote
   leg `AddHost` drives (inverse register, reconcile, install), or only for the
   registration whose success `host add` prints?
2. Should an exit code from a transport that cannot be trusted to carry one be
   demoted to a hint everywhere, or only inside `AddHost`?
3. Per this repo's own style rules this is a **correctness gap, not a request
   for defensive coding**: the code currently believes a signal that is provably
   wrong, and reading back the state it just wrote is an assertion about reality,
   not a guard against an impossible state.

Note the scope trap: upgrading `tailscaled` on `yasyf-home` fixes the symptom on
this one pair and leaves synckit trusting an unreliable signal on every other
peer, including any peer that later downgrades or runs a different SSH server.

## Adjacent verified fact — `host add`'s bootstrap leg is NOT the sealed contract

This will confuse the next reader, so it is recorded here deliberately.

`daemon/host.go:40` → `hostregistry/transport.go:92-94` (`execRunner.SSH`) →
`ExecBootstrapSSH` (`hostregistry/dial.go:93-98`) → `execSSHOnce`
(`dial.go:134-151`), whose entire option set is `dialOpts` at
`hostregistry/dial.go:31-36`:

```go
var dialOpts = []string{
	"-o", "BatchMode=yes",
	"-o", "ConnectTimeout=3",
	"-o", "ServerAliveInterval=5",
	"-o", "ServerAliveCountMax=3",
}
```

No `-F /dev/null`, no `StrictHostKeyChecking`, no `HostKeyAlias`. So the
bootstrap leg inherits `~/.ssh/config`, which on this machine carries a
`Host *` block with `StrictHostKeyChecking no` (`~/.ssh/config:9`) — the
bootstrap leg blind-TOFUs.

The sealed contract is `RemoteSSHArgv` at `hostregistry/ssh_contract.go:74-120`
(`-F /dev/null`, `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`, pinned `UserKnownHostsFile`,
`HostKeyAlias`, `IdentitiesOnly`, no agent/proxy/forwarding), and it governs only
the **runtime** transport. `ExecBootstrapSSH`'s own doc comment says as much:
"It never participates in runtime service transport."

(Anchor corrections: the caller is `hostregistry/transport.go:92-94`, not
`daemon/transport.go:92` — `daemon/transport.go` is 54 lines and resolves typed
sync transports, not ssh. `AddHost` is invoked at `daemon/host.go:40`.)

**Whether that split is intended deserves an explicit answer in this record.**
The bootstrap leg runs before a host fact exists, so it cannot use a
`HostKeyAlias` it has not learned yet — that much is structural. What is not
obviously intended is that it silently adopts the user's `~/.ssh/config`, so the
security posture of the one leg that establishes trust is set by a file outside
synckit.

ops.text: A host add whose inverse-registration leg fails is reported as a failure, not as 'registered inverse host … reconciled … installed services'
Success of a remote mutating leg is corroborated by reading the peer state back, not inferred from the ssh exit code alone
The owner has answered, in this record, whether host add's bootstrap leg inheriting ~/.ssh/config (no -F /dev/null, no StrictHostKeyChecking, no HostKeyAlias) is intended
A regression test covers a transport that returns exit 0 for a remote command that actually failed
